Quick update:
- Confirmed elevated 502/503/504s from the regional edge LB in us-east-1 between 07:38–08:10 PT.
- Upstream service (inference runtime) error rates are normal; errors appear at the LB/edge layer with increased connection resets and short-lived 504s.
- Evidence of retry amplification: client SDKs are configured for aggressive retries, which amplified load during the window.

Attached: lb_access_20260309_partial.log (sanitized)

Working next: capture tcpdump for failed flows and coordinate with infra provider.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.example>, PrIyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/503/504s across US edge — immediate impact

Folks — no control-plane deploys in the last 24 hours. However, we had an autoscaling event that increased LB worker churn after a health-check misclassification (flapping) around 07:35. Provider telemetry shows a short window where edge routing table convergence lagged (~90s) which can cause 502/503 from the edge.

Recommendation: drain affected LB instances for forced reprovision + enable secondary routing pool for Acme tenant. Also suggest immediate change: temporarily increase client-side retry backoff for Acme to reduce amplification.

-Monica
Infra Ops
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, csm@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.example>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.example>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/503/504s across US edge — immediate impact

Alex — recap and immediate mitigations we applied:
- Forced drain + reprovision of 3 edge instances in us-east-1 that showed flapping health checks.
- Activated secondary routing pool for Acme tenant (traffic began shifting at 09:05 PT).
- Asked your SRE to increase client retry backoff; we also pushed a per-tenant throttling rule to limit request concurrency for Acme to 60% of baseline while we stabilize.

We expect reduced errors within 20–30 minutes and will monitor closely. Marcus will share logs and a post-incident summary.

Apologies for the disruption — cc'ing Evelyn (VP Sales) given exec visibility.

Best,
Vanessa
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>

Please send incident write-up and any mitigations for our internal post-mortem and our CIO briefing. We'll need an RCA and any steps to prevent retry amplification in future.

Alex

Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 502/503/504s across US edge — immediate impact

Final incident summary (short):
- Impact window: 07:38–09:20 PT on 2026-03-09. Root cause: edge load balancer instance health-check flapping during autoscaling event, causing transient routing table inconsistencies in us-east-1.
- Contributing factor: aggressive client retry behavior amplified load, producing a retry storm that worsened LB saturation.
- Mitigations applied: drained and reprovisioned flapping LB instances; enabled secondary routing pool for Acme; applied per-tenant concurrency throttle; recommended client retry backoff.
- Next steps: permanent fix for LB health-check sensitivity (infra change), add auto-throttle for suspected retry storms, and a tenant-level circuit-breaker option we can offer customers.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf (proposed timeline for hardening and credits)

Jonas Weber
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
